_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the only thing that ever promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, behind its own pull request — see that file's own doc comment for why the human checkpoint lives there instead of here. Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved' (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). A human's actual review happens by reading/merging the review agent's PR, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
suggestions.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thebusinessdesk.com, wilmslow.co.uk/alderleyedge.com and the operator's own site (firestationsocial.co.uk): Fire Station Social Cucina, 75 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY, opened 10 June 2026 in the former Gusto unit — the second site for this specific concept, after the original in Tarporley. Run by 'Project Social Cucina', the restaurant division of Cheshire Pub Company (a separate entity from the 7-pub Cheshire Cat group already referenced elsewhere in this file) — only 2 sites confirmed under the Fire Station Social Cucina name itself, the same 2-site sibling precedent already used for Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello. Flagged for the reviewer: the parent company's own press describes this as 'expansion', so worth a quick re-check at promotion time that a third site hasn't since appeared. Moderate-high confidence otherwise — real, recently opened, well-covered locally, no closure signals. Re-checked again 2026-09-08 (curia-suggestion-review daily pass) specifically for a rumoured third site: none found — same 2-site status as this note originally recorded, still pending, still in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than re-decided here. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session: promoted into venues.json with the new `status: 'coming-soon'` field (added the same day specifically for this case) rather than a flat yes/no — real venue, passes Hard rule 1 on site count today, but its editorial confidence marker stays provisional given the parent's stated expansion plans. See venues.json's own note on the new field.

suggestions.name: Bramall Hall
suggestions.reason: Grade I timber-framed since the Tudors, the Great Hall's carved screen and an Elizabethan plaster ceiling under one roof — the exterior scaffolding comes down by the end of the year, but the period rooms have been open behind it the whole time.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via stockport.gov.uk, historichouses.org and tripadvisor.com: Bramall Hall, SK7 3NX, a Grade I-listed Tudor manor in 70 acres of parkland, owned by Stockport Metropolitan Borough Council since 1935 (bought from the Davenport family) and run as a public visitor attraction with its own dedicated opening hours — a real, non-commercial civic asset, the same precedent as Fletcher Moss Botanical Garden/Thorn Grove Park/Marie Louise Gardens elsewhere in this file, so no chain-footprint question applies. Currently under exterior roof-restoration scaffolding (due off by end of 2026 per stockport.gov.uk) but the Hall and Visitor Centre remain open on their normal published hours throughout — not a closure signal. Bramhall's first Do-category candidate; the district currently has zero venues. Introduces a new type, HISTORIC HOUSE — the existing HERITAGE CENTRE type (Knutsford Heritage Centre) reads as a smaller volunteer-run local-history exhibit, not the walk-through-period-rooms register of a stately home museum, so a dedicated type fits better; category-only (Do) for now, same treatment as FARM EXPERIENCE/BOOKSHOP elsewhere in this file since no onboarding tile fits precisely. High confidence — real, currently operating, unambiguous single civic ownership.

suggestions.name: The Mounting Stone
suggestions.reason: Six cask lines in a converted Bramhall blacksmith's, two of them always Bollington, and a house microbrewery upstairs of the cellar renamed Bramhall Beers this year — keep it small and keep it simple, exactly as the pub promises.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk), whatpub.com and Stockport & South Manchester CAMRA branch pages: The Mounting Stone, 8 Woodford Road, Bramhall SK7 1JJ, a micropub open since June 2016 in a former blacksmith's, with its own in-house microbrewery (Made of Stone, renamed Bramhall Beers in early 2025). It's the sister pub to Cheadle Hulme's Chiverton Tap (also suggested in this batch) under the same small ethos — a real 2-site sibling pair, the same precedent already established for Cibo/Suburban Green/Wallop elsewhere in this file, not a chain. No closure signals found; CAMRA listing and recent Tripadvisor reviews both current. Reused the existing ALE HOUSE type (The Chorlton Tap/The Beer House/The Seven Oaks) rather than introducing a new one — a real-ale-led micropub is exactly that register. Bramhall's first Drink-category candidate. High confidence.

suggestions.name: Pix Pizza
suggestions.reason: Dough proved for seventy-two hours and hand-stretched before the wood oven gets it, ingredients sourced direct from Italy where it counts — Bramhall Village Square's own room, not the Altrincham takeaway's twin.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via tripadvisor.com, restaurantguru.com and pixpizza.co.uk: Pix Pizza, 14-15 Bramhall Centre, Bramhall Lane South, Bramhall (Village Square), open Wednesday-Sunday, wood-fired Roman/Neapolitan-method pizza. Confirmed exactly 2 sites — this dine-in restaurant in Bramhall and a separate takeaway-only outlet at 19 Shaw's Road, Altrincham (WA14 1QU) — the same small-sibling-pair precedent already used for Craig's/Ivy Spinningfields/Cibo elsewhere in this file, not a chain. No closure signals; rated 5/5 on Tripadvisor as of this search, active social media. Reused the existing PIZZERIA type (Rudy's, Altrincham). Bramhall's first Eat-category candidate — with this, Bramall Hall and The Mounting Stone (also in this batch), Bramhall moves from 0 venues to a first real spread across all three categories. High confidence.

suggestions.name: The Chiverton Tap
suggestions.reason: An award-winning micropub in a converted draper's shop on Mellor Road — the original half of the same small pair as Bramhall's own Mounting Stone, and no less serious about the cask.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via whatpub.com, Tripadvisor and Yelp: The Chiverton Tap, 8 Mellor Road, Cheadle Hulme SK8 5AU, an award-winning micropub in a converted drapers shop, sister pub (and the original) to Bramhall's The Mounting Stone (also suggested in this batch) — a real 2-site sibling pair, not a chain, same precedent as Wallop/Cibo elsewhere in this file. No closure signals; live drinks board (thechivertontap.co.uk) and recent reviews both current. Reused the existing ALE HOUSE type. Cheadle Hulme's Drink category is currently its joint-weakest (2 of 7, alongside Eat) — this closes part of that gap. High confidence.

suggestions.name: Dos Hermanos
suggestions.reason: Head chef Carlos's Spanish tapas inside a building raised in 1899 on Mellor Road — the authentic plates Cheadle Hulme didn't have until this year.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Companies House (Dos Hermanos Tapas Ltd, incorporated April 2024), the operator's own site (doshermanos.bar) and Tripadvisor (ranked #4 of 23 Cheadle Hulme restaurants): Dos Hermanos Tapas & Bar, 1 Mellor Road, Cheadle Hulme SK8 5AT, a single-site independent Spanish tapas restaurant in a building dating to 1899. No sibling or chain footprint found anywhere — confirmed single-site. No closure signals; active bookings/reviews. Mapped to the existing SMALL PLATES type (tapas is the same sharing-plates register as Victors/Volta elsewhere in this file). Cheadle Hulme's Eat category is currently its joint-weakest (2 of 7) — this closes part of that gap. High confidence.

suggestions.name: Staircase House
suggestions.reason: A rare Jacobean cage-newel staircase — one of only three left in the country — inside a fifteenth-century townhouse on Market Place, sixteen rooms walking you from 1460 to the 1940s without leaving the building.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via stockport.gov.uk and artuk.org: Staircase House, 30/31 Market Place, Stockport SK1 1ES, a council-run 15th-century townhouse museum with published 2026 opening hours (Wed-Sun, closed Mon/Tue). Real civic attraction, same non-commercial precedent as Bramall Hall (also in this batch) and Fletcher Moss Botanical Garden elsewhere in this file — no chain-footprint question applies. No closure signals; current 2026 opening-hours page confirms it's operating now. Uses the same new HISTORIC HOUSE type introduced for Bramall Hall in this batch, for the same reasoning (a walk-through period-rooms museum, distinct from the smaller volunteer-run HERITAGE CENTRE register). Stockport (Underbanks)'s Do category is currently its weakest (1 of 4, alongside Drink) — this closes part of that gap. High confidence.

suggestions.name: The Underbank
suggestions.reason: A former Cheshire bank on Great Underbank turned beer hall, Pomona Island and Runaway on tap and Stockport's first proper sound system in the basement — the same husband-and-wife team behind Heaton Moor's Nook, just considerably louder.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via manchestersfinest.com, confidentials.com and Stockport Nub News: The Underbank, 27 Great Underbank, Stockport SK1 1LN, opened 30 May 2025 in a former bank building by Des and Nina O'Malley, who also run Nook in Heaton Moor — a real 2-site sibling pair, not a chain, same precedent as Bar Caput's own operator-relaunch treatment and Wallop/Cibo elsewhere in this file. Coordinates approximated from the same Great Underbank street as the already-seeded Bar Caput (postcode-level geocoding tools were unreachable this run) rather than invented from scratch. FLAG FOR RE-CHECK: one search summary described 'Underbank Bar Stockport' as showing a closed-style Tripadvisor attraction listing, which reads as a stale/mismatched aggregator entry (an 'Underbank Weekender' festival and an unrelated 'Underbank' place name in South Yorkshire and Australia surfaced in the same searches, likely conflated) rather than a real closure signal for this specific venue — a live open-mic listing (Undercurrent at The Underbank) and the venue's own still-active site/socials point to it currently trading, but the reviewer should re-verify directly given the mixed signal before promoting. Mapped to the existing LATE-NIGHT LOUNGE type (DJ sets/soundsystem focus, closest fit to Symposium's register) rather than introducing a new one. Moderate confidence given the flagged ambiguity above.

suggestions.name: Sett174 Art Cafe
suggestions.reason: A West Didsbury art cafe with a secret garden out back for the resin and graffiti classes, and local artists' work on every wall instead of online — coffee and a biscuit if you'd rather just watch.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via ilovemanchester.com, creativetourist.com and Manchester City Council's own licensing register: Sett174 Art Cafe, 174 Burton Road, West Didsbury M20 1LH, opened by Frank Clarke as a hands-on art space/cafe with a walled 'secret garden' used for its graffiti and resin art classes. Single independent site, no sibling or chain footprint found. Currently trading — active Eventbrite listing for upcoming activities and live Instagram/Facebook as of this search; no closure signals. Introduces a new type, ART STUDIO — closer in spirit to the existing 'Cookery & craft' tile register (Knutcraft's pottery classes) than to a pure viewing gallery (ART GALLERY), given the hands-on-class focus; category-only (Do) for now, same treatment as BOOKSHOP/FARM EXPERIENCE elsewhere in this file. Didsbury's Do category is currently tied-weakest (2 of 7, alongside Drink). Moderate-high confidence — opening hours had some inconsistency between sources, otherwise clean.

suggestions.name: The Creameries
suggestions.reason: Pomona Island's bakery, bar and kitchen where Blanchflower used to be on Wilbraham Road — sixteen keg lines, six of them reserved for wine, and bread proofing somewhere behind the counter all morning.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via manchesterwire.co.uk, confidentials.com and tasteofmanchester.com: The Creameries, 406 Wilbraham Road, Chorlton M21 0SD, reopened 29 April 2026 as a bakery/café-bar/kitchen by Pomona Island Brew Co. (independent Salford craft brewery), in the unit most recently home to Blanchflower. Pomona Island also runs a brew-tap in Salford and a pub, North Westward Ho, in Manchester city centre — a 3-site footprint under one small independent brewery, at the outer edge of but still consistent with this file's existing small-sibling-group precedent (Wallop's own 3-site Knutsford/Prestwich/Didsbury group). No closure signals; active 2026 reviews and coverage. Mapped to the existing GASTROPUB type (food-plus-drink hybrid register, same as FOLK/Wilmslow Tavern) rather than introducing a new one, though it reads more café-bakery than pub — closest existing fit. Chorlton's Eat category is currently its weakest (2 of 8). Moderate-high confidence given the 3-site footprint is worth the reviewer's own judgment call.

suggestions.name: Prana
suggestions.reason: Two floors of proper acoustics on Ashley Road from the team behind Stockport's Amp — order the cocktail, but the stage is the reason to stay past nine.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA (camra.org.uk), whatpub.com and Altrincham Today: Prana, 14-16 Ashley Road, Altrincham WA14 2DW, an independent live-music venue and cocktail bar opened November 2023, run by the same team as Amp in Stockport — a real 2-site sibling pair, not a chain, same precedent as Bramhall/Cheadle Hulme's Mounting Stone/Chiverton Tap pair in this batch. No closure signals; CAMRA-listed and actively promoted. Mapped to the existing COCKTAIL BAR type (it is explicitly a cocktail bar first, live-music venue second, per its own billing) rather than the Do-category LIVE MUSIC type, since Altrincham's Drink category is currently its weakest (2 of 9) and this venue's own framing supports the Drink read. High confidence.
